newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-North looks for future growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-North looks for future growth.

text.p: Australian mining and forestry group North Ltd said on Thursday it expected trading to be flat in 1996/97, but saw profits improving further out as new projects came on-stream.
Chairman Michael Deeley told the annual general meeting the current year was being restrained by the subdued prospects for commodity prices, but said the company had a solid base.
"Given average market conditions, this together with developments in the pipeline should lift profits substantially by 1998/99 and beyond," he said.
North reported a net profit of A$111.89 million in the year to June 30, 1996, down from A$116.37 million in 1994/95.

Managing director Campbell Anderson later told reporters that North expected substantial profits from its 25 percent interest in the Alumbrera gold and copper project in Argentina, even at current copper prices.
"When we went into Alumbrera, we did not assume a long run copper price significantly higher than the present one," he said.
The project, which is due to begin production from August 1997, is expected to produce 180,000 tonnes of copper and 640,000 ounces of gold a year.
MIM Holdings Ltd chief executive Nick Stump said last week that the massive gold credits meant the net copper cost of the Alumbrera project was below 30 U.S. cents a pound.
MIM is 50 percent owner and operator of Alumbrera, while North and Rio Algom Ltd each own 25 percent.
Anderson also said North expected U.S. sales for its Robe River iron ore operation to fall in the current year and that South Korean sales would remain steady.
Sales to Japan were expected to improve as its steel sector recovered, and Robe would continue to explore market opportunities in China and the surrounding region, he said.
Robe River, in Western Australia, contributed A$109.4 million to North's group earnings in 1995/96, down 8.6 percent on the previous year, despite a production increase of 6.5 percent.
North also expected flat earnings from its 68 percent-owned uranium miner Energy Resources of Australia Ltd (ERA) this year, but with a significant increase in earnings after that.
Anderson said uranium oxide sales would be flat or a little down on last year and this would be only broadly offset by any price improvement.

ERA said said earlier this month its production outlook was the brightest it had been for 15 years and that the recent rise in international uranium oxide prices would allow the company to proceed with new capital investment.
North's share price closed down one cent at A$3.59.
